subject.title: [Security] Environment variable leak through untrusted code execution in Crabbox

question: Does the reporter have a concrete current-main reproduction showing a sensitive value reaching untrusted Crabbox execution despite the existing explicit-forwarding and clean-host controls?
rationale: Without the variable name, its source, and a sanitized child-environment transcript, the review cannot distinguish an OpenClaw boundary bypass from benign host variables or externally provisioned runner state.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Ask for a private GHSA containing the exact variable source, sanitized launch command, child observation, and current-main SHA before selecting a remediation boundary.

options.title: Close as unsupported
options.body: Close if no concrete secret-bearing variable or current-main propagation path can be supplied after security review.

recommendation.title: Request private reproduction
recommendation.body: Ask for a private GHSA containing the exact variable source, sanitized launch command, child observation, and current-main SHA before selecting a remediation boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this account to recent Crabbox integration and workflow decisions.
